Cardiovascular Physiology Notes

Volumes and output

Stroke volume is the volume of blood ejected by one ventricle during a single contraction.

Cardiac output equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume.

Ejection fraction is the proportion of end diastolic volume that is ejected with each beat.

Loading conditions

Preload is the stretch of ventricular muscle at the end of diastole before contraction begins.

Afterload is the resistance the ventricle must overcome to eject blood into the aorta.

Pressure

Mean arterial pressure is approximately diastolic pressure plus one third of the pulse pressure.
